card-11a-streamer-myth.title: A highlight reel isn’t a balance sheet.

referenceNotes.title: A highlight reel isn’t a balance sheet.
referenceNotes.body: A winning clip can show only part of the record. Add all stakes and returns before drawing a conclusion about profit.
referenceNotes.scope: Use a clearly named period and include losses, costs and time. A selected win does not establish a profitable pattern or promise a future result.

referenceNotes.title: “My numbers are due.”
referenceNotes.body: Example: six different numbers drawn uniformly from 49. Each complete combination has the same full-match probability.
referenceNotes.scope: Restore all 49 numbers before each independent draw: past draws do not change the next chance. Within one draw, balls are not replaced. This is not the chance of any prize in every lottery.

card-13a-its-due.title: A losing streak isn’t a countdown.

referenceNotes.title: A losing streak isn’t a countdown.
referenceNotes.body: For independent spins, past losses don’t make the next win closer.
referenceNotes.scope: This assumes unchanged rules and game state. A retained feature needs its own rules. Theoretical return is not a repayment schedule for earlier losses.

referenceNotes.title: Close on screen. Check the actual prize.

referenceNotes.title: Plan a content evaluation
referenceNotes.body: Test whether readers understand the message and can find its intended next action. Ratings help diagnose content; they do not demonstrate safer gambling or reduced harm.
referenceNotes.scope: Fix factual errors, inaccessible actions and harmful misunderstandings before wider use. Record what changed, then retest. There is no universal score that approves a resource for publication.

sections.title: 1. Define the test
sections.body: Name the resource version, audience, language, placement and primary question. Agree recruitment, consent, data handling, sample rationale, timing, comparison and decision criteria before collecting responses.

sections.title: 2. Pulse: initial feedback
sections.body: Ask an optional recommendation question (0–10), a Forgettable–Memorable rating (1–7) and one thing to change. Add a separate comprehension or next-action task when that is the question you need to answer.

sections.title: 3. Full: diagnose the experience
sections.body: Use the recommendation question, five ratings and open feedback. Pairs: Forgettable–Memorable; Boring–Engaging; Preachy–Respectful; Confusing–Clear; Generic–Made for me. These content questions need pretesting.

sections.title: 4. Recall: follow up
sections.body: Choose an interval that fits the question. Ask for unprompted recall before two scoped knowledge checks, then optional self-reported follow-through. Record invited, reached and completed counts; do not assume a response rate.

sections.title: 5. Interpret within scope
sections.body: NPS = percentage rating 9–10 minus percentage rating 0–6. Ratings of 7–8 stay in the denominator. Exclude missing answers and report their count. A 1–7 scale has midpoint 4, not a validated pass mark.

sections.title: 6. Report and decide
sections.body: Report each item’s valid count, response distribution, recruitment, limitations and negative findings. No fixed sample size proves adequacy. For comparisons, plan precision or power and uncertainty; do not declare a winner from a higher average alone.

referenceNotes.scope: Before confirming, check the covered accounts and venues, start date, duration and whether cancellation or shortening is allowed. Review the return process and how existing funds or bets are handled.

referenceNotes.title: You can ask for support.
referenceNotes.body: For questions about your gambling or someone else’s, choose a contact method below.
referenceNotes.scope: Ask the service about eligibility, costs and how your information is handled.

referenceNotes.title: Five things staff should know
referenceNotes.body: Use your organisation’s actual tools, contacts and procedures.
referenceNotes.scope: If you do not know the answer, say so and find the responsible person or verified source.

sections.title: 1. Know the tools
sections.body: Locate the actual limits, reminders and activity views. Explain what each covers and its limitations.

sections.title: 2. Speak plainly
sections.body: Use words the person understands. Explain terms without labelling or diagnosing them.

sections.title: 3. Verify the contacts
sections.body: Check who each service supports, its hours, costs, privacy terms and available contact channels.

sections.title: 4. Offer support discreetly
sections.body: Ask whether the person would like contact details. Follow your organisation’s privacy and escalation procedures.

sections.title: 5. Show the information
sections.body: Point to the relevant game rules and player resources. Use the current version and check the destination.

referenceNotes.title: Double-zero roulette
referenceNotes.body: A standard double-zero wheel has 38 pockets. Standard bets have this house edge, except the five-number basket (0, 00, 1, 2, 3) paying 6:1.
referenceNotes.scope: That 6:1 basket has 7.89% edge. Check the wheel, payout and zero rules; variants change the calculation.

referenceNotes.title: Same stake. Different returns.
referenceNotes.body: Each example is a winning $100.00 cash bet. Total return includes the original stake.
referenceNotes.scope: Profit is the amount above the stake. Examples exclude deductions and promotional adjustments. A losing bet loses the stake; check the accepted price and settlement rules.

referenceNotes.title: “I’m on a hot streak.”
referenceNotes.body: In an independent-round model with unchanged rules and state, previous wins do not change the next round’s probabilities. A retained feature state needs its own rules.
referenceNotes.scope: A run of wins does not create a need for another bet. Check which features carry over and how their rules work.

referenceNotes.title: Your account tools
referenceNotes.body: Use the options your service actually provides. Check their terms before confirming a change.
referenceNotes.scope: A reminder, account pause and self-exclusion have different effects. Check each option’s terms and effective time.

referenceNotes.title: Withdrawal request received
referenceNotes.body: Example request: $150.00. Receipt is not confirmation that payment has arrived.
referenceNotes.scope: Check your request’s status, reference, method and expected timing. Session net is returns minus stakes here; it excludes deposits, withdrawals, fees and bonuses. A withdrawal is not itself profit.

referenceNotes.title: Know the game. Then make your call.
referenceNotes.body: Rules, payouts, house edge. Three things to check before you play.
referenceNotes.scope: Match the information to the actual game, bet and rules. An average house edge does not predict one session.

referenceNotes.title: The paytable is worth a look.
referenceNotes.body: See what each result pays. Check return-to-player information where it is provided.
referenceNotes.scope: RTP describes an average over many plays. It is not the chance of a prize or a promised return for your session.

poster-19e-never-due.title: A losing run is not a countdown.

referenceNotes.title: A losing run is not a countdown.
referenceNotes.body: Past losses do not make the next independent slot spin more likely to win.
referenceNotes.scope: This assumes unchanged rules and game state. Features that carry state need their own explanation; RTP is not a repayment deadline.

referenceNotes.title: Pick an amount. Choose a limit period.
referenceNotes.body: Check what the deposit limit covers, when it resets and when changes take effect.
referenceNotes.scope: Use the tools actually available in your account. A deposit limit may not cover cash gambling or every form of spending.

referenceNotes.title: A budget is a limit. Not a spending target.
referenceNotes.body: Choose an amount you can afford to spend on entertainment. You can leave some or all of it unspent.
referenceNotes.scope: You can choose not to gamble. A budget does not guarantee a particular result or make losses recoverable.

poster-19h-time-flies.title: Choose when to call it a night.

referenceNotes.title: Choose the end time before the start.
referenceNotes.body: If a reminder is available, set it for when you want to finish. Check in when it arrives.
referenceNotes.scope: Check how the feature works. A reminder does not automatically end a session unless the product actually does that.

referenceNotes.title: Birthdays get no special odds.
referenceNotes.body: In a fair draw of six different numbers from 49, every six-number combination has the same full-match chance: 1 in 13,983,816.
referenceNotes.scope: This is one illustrative draw format. Full-match odds differ from any-prize odds; check the actual lottery rules.
